type: extension (post-Gate-B, from CANDIDATE_SELECTION_AUDIT.md; user authorised justified additions 2026-10-30)
rationale: Hierarchical vs flat strategies mixes unit size with parent expansion; a children-only control on identical children and vectors isolates the small-to-big expansion effect.
pipeline: pymupdf_layout -> hierarchical 200/40 children -> intfloat/e5-small-v2 dense ranking (shared vector cache with RQ2-v2/RQ4-v2) -> assembly.

arms.hierarchical: production assembly: deduplicated parents in rank order, +-200-word windowing for parents > 800 tokens, 1,600 est. tokens, <= 5 units
arms.children_only: the same ranked children assembled as flat units, 1,600 est. tokens, <= 5 units, no parent expansion

primary: CEC@0.5, children_only vs hierarchical, single comparison, paper-cluster paired bootstrap B=10,000 seed 42
secondary: CEC at tau 0.3 and 0.7, context tokens, units per context; nDCG@10 reported per arm but not compared (relevance units differ: children vs parents)
metric_note: CEC is primary here regardless of the RQ2-v2 CEC fallback rule, because nDCG is not comparable across these arms. If the 30-case CEC check falls below 80% agreement, this result is reported with that caveat.
decision_rule: Descriptive only; never adopted (it would remove parent expansion). It informs the wording of the RQ2 conclusion only.
caveat: children_only contexts are smaller (<= 5 children of ~200 tokens), so the difference is the combined effect of expansion and the extra context it supplies, which is what small-to-big means in production.
timing: Runs together with RQ2-v2, after the CEC labels and the 80% rule.
precision_rule: Planned CI half-width as RQ2 (~0.035). If observed is larger: report and propose, do not expand.
